doc.title: Wendy Oxenhorn — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Born in Brooklyn; grandparents' stories
summary: She recalls early Brooklyn memories, the move to Westchester, and her immigrant grandfathers and grandmother.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Sure. I don’t remember much, because we moved, I think, when I was 5 years old. I do remember, though, it was not far from Coney Island, and I remember tricycling on the boardwalk. I remember there not being many trees, and missing that feeling of... I loved anything connected with Nature. There were honeysuckle bushes that grew right alongside our apartment building, and that was my big thrill, to be able to go and pick the honeysuckle, and taste the little honey and sniff it. I remember... I wonder if that’s how my parents ended up deciding, “maybe we should get this kid into the country.” I don’t know. But we moved to little apartments in Westchester, and there my life got much bigger.
You were just showing us photos of your parents, your grandparents. Can you tell us about your own genealogical bloodline?

Sure. We’re a good mix. I know we have a big gypsy side to us. I found out Grandfather Oxenhorn was born in Romania. Actually, we think it was even Transylvania. The other grandfather was born in Russia. They left... I think he was 16. I know he almost drowned. He had to escape in a river, and an old man saved his life, because he was drowning. He came to this country, and became a Charleston champion. There’s the dancer connect. He was an incredible, self-made man. He ended up with three jobs. He would take my grandmother to the opera and do wonderful things with her. I know they were very poor, but he always would do beautiful things. He was an amazing man. I have very fond memories of him.
I think you said the other grandfather was a doctor?
He had a pharmacy. I never met that grandfather.

Yeah. I did. I stole her Parliament cigarettes actually when we would go on family visits. She’d keep them under the mattress. Went in the bathroom, smoke a cigarette. I think I was 10. I would go in after her, because it still smelled of smoke, and no one would suspect me, and I would smoke Parliaments. I’m very sentimental about Parliaments.
